HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 48-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.49, creatinine 0.81-0.84, hemoglobin 10.8-12.2, platelets 292-296, sodium 138-139, wbc 8.2-8.6; vitals dbp 67-71, heart_rate 78-80, map 88-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 129-132, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.82-0.84, hemoglobin 9.7-10.7, platelets 291-299, sodium 138-139, wbc 7.9-8.2; vitals dbp 67-72, heart_rate 74-79, map 87-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 124-131, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 48-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
